questions.passage: Modern laptops are no longer just portable computers. They have become all-in-one productivity hubs with features like facial recognition login, OLED touchscreens, and built-in AI assistants. Battery technology has also improved significantly, with some models offering over 20 hours of usage on a single charge. Manufacturers are now competing not just on processing speed, but on thinness, weight, and thermal efficiency.

options: A. Laptop batteries now last more than 20 hours on a single charge.
B. Modern laptops have evolved into versatile, feature-rich devices that rival desktop computers.

D. Manufacturers prioritize thinness over performance in modern laptop design.

questions.passage: Artificial intelligence is no longer confined to research laboratories. It is now embedded in everyday tools such as email filters, music recommendation algorithms, navigation apps, and smart home devices. Most users interact with AI dozens of times a day without realizing it. This quiet integration into daily life marks a significant shift from AI being a futuristic concept to becoming an invisible layer of modern infrastructure.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. Smart home devices are the most advanced form of artificial intelligence available today.
B. AI research laboratories are becoming more accessible to the general public.
C. Artificial intelligence has quietly become embedded in the everyday tools people use.
D. Music recommendation algorithms are the most widely used AI application worldwide.

questions.passage: Cloud gaming is challenging the traditional model of video game ownership. Instead of purchasing expensive consoles or high-end gaming PCs, players can now stream games directly to any screen through services like Xbox Cloud Gaming and NVIDIA GeForce Now. This shift reduces hardware barriers for new gamers but raises concerns about internet dependency and data privacy, since all game processing happens on remote servers rather than local devices.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. Xbox Cloud Gaming and NVIDIA GeForce Now are the two dominant platforms in the gaming industry.
B. Cloud gaming is transforming how people access and play video games by removing the need for expensive hardware.
C. Data privacy is the biggest threat to the future of the cloud gaming industry.
D. Smartphones are replacing consoles as the preferred device for gaming worldwide.

questions.passage: Wearable health technology has expanded far beyond simple step counters. Smartwatches can now monitor blood oxygen levels, detect irregular heart rhythms, measure skin temperature, and even perform electrocardiograms. Some devices alert users to potential health conditions before symptoms appear, effectively turning everyday accessories into passive medical monitoring tools. Researchers are exploring whether continuous wearable data could eventually assist in early detection of conditions like diabetes and atrial fibrillation.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. Smartwatches are now capable of detecting diabetes and atrial fibrillation in all users.
B. Wearable health technology has advanced significantly and now functions as a personal medical monitoring tool.
C. Electrocardiograms performed by smartwatches are more accurate than those done in hospitals.
D. Step counters remain the most popular feature of modern smartwatches.

questions.passage: The rise of quantum computing poses a serious threat to current encryption standards. Most online security systems today rely on the difficulty of factoring large prime numbers, a task that classical computers cannot complete in any reasonable timeframe. Quantum computers could theoretically solve such problems in seconds, rendering widely used encryption protocols like RSA obsolete. Governments and cybersecurity firms are now racing to develop post-quantum cryptography before quantum hardware becomes powerful enough to break existing systems.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. RSA encryption is already broken by current quantum computers available on the market.
B. Factoring large prime numbers is the primary method used to build quantum computers.
C. Quantum computing threatens existing encryption systems, driving urgent development of new security standards.
D. Governments are building their own quantum computers to replace those made by private companies.

questions.passage: E-waste has become one of the fastest-growing environmental problems linked to the technology industry. As consumers upgrade devices more frequently due to rapid product cycles, millions of tons of discarded smartphones, laptops, and accessories end up in landfills each year. Many of these devices contain toxic materials such as lead, mercury, and cadmium that can leach into soil and groundwater. Despite recycling programs offered by major brands, only a small fraction of global e-waste is properly processed, leaving significant environmental and health risks unaddressed.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. Lead, mercury, and cadmium are the three most dangerous chemicals found in electronic devices.
B. E-waste is a growing environmental crisis caused by rapid technology consumption and inadequate recycling.
C. Major tech brands are the primary cause of environmental destruction through their recycling programs.
D. Consumers should stop upgrading their devices in order to solve the e-waste problem.

questions.passage: Smartphones today are equipped with processors that outperform computers from just a decade ago. The Apple A17 Pro chip, for example, features a 3-nanometer architecture that allows billions of transistors to fit within a space smaller than a fingernail. This level of miniaturization enables smartphones to handle tasks such as real-time video editing, on-device machine learning, and augmented reality applications without relying on cloud servers. Despite this processing power, manufacturers continue to face challenges in battery capacity, since energy demands grow faster than battery technology can keep up.

questions.passage: Generative AI tools have fundamentally changed how creative professionals work. Graphic designers now use AI platforms such as Adobe Firefly and Midjourney to produce initial concept drafts in minutes rather than hours. questions.passage: The Great Barrier Reef, located off the coast of Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system. It is composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and stretches for over 2,300 kilometers. Scientists have observed that the reef is currently facing significant threats due to climate change, specifically rising ocean temperatures, which lead to 'coral bleaching.' When corals are stressed by heat, they expel the algae living in their tissues, causing them to turn completely white. While the reef is a protected marine park, local pollution from agricultural runoff and coastal development continue to challenge conservation efforts.

questions.passage: Electric vehicles (EVs) are rapidly reshaping the automotive industry as nations strive to reduce carbon emissions. Powered by rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs, EVs produce zero tailpipe emissions, making them a cleaner alternative to traditional internal combustion engine vehicles. However, the widespread adoption of EVs faces several hurdles, including the high cost of battery manufacturing, limited driving range per charge, and the current scarcity of public charging infrastructure. Despite these challenges, continuous advancements in battery technology and increasing government subsidies are expected to accelerate EV adoption over the next decade.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: A. Lithium-ion batteries are the only efficient way to power modern vehicles.
B. The automotive industry is completely stopping the production of gas-powered cars.
C. Government subsidies are the sole reason why people buy electric vehicles.
D. Electric vehicles are transforming transportation, though they still face infrastructure and cost challenges.

questions.passage: The Renaissance was a fervent period of European cultural, artistic, political, and scientific 'rebirth' following the Middle Ages. Promoted by a rediscovery of classical philosophy, literature, and art, it produced some of the world's greatest thinkers and creators, including Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. This era fundamentally shifted human perspective from a strictly religious worldview to humanism, which emphasized individual potential and agency. The intellectual movement eventually paved the way for the Scientific Revolution and the dawn of the modern world.
questions.question: What is the primary topic of the passage?
options: A. The artistic rivalry between Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo.
B. An overview of the Renaissance period and its cultural and intellectual impact.
C. The economic systems that funded the European Middle Ages.
D. How the Scientific Revolution directly ended religious beliefs in Europe.

questions.passage: Deep-sea hydrothermal vents are fissures on the ocean floor that geothermally heat water. Unlike most ecosystems on Earth that rely on sunlight for energy through photosynthesis, hydrothermal vent communities depend on chemosynthesis. Bacteria in these vents use toxic chemical compounds, such as hydrogen sulfide, to produce energy, forming the base of a unique food web. This discovery proved to scientists that highly complex life forms can thrive in absolute darkness and under extreme hydrostatic pressure, altering our understanding of life's boundaries.
questions.question: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: A. Hydrothermal vents are dangerous fissures that destroy marine ecosystems.
B. Photosynthesis remains the only reliable process to sustain life forms on the ocean floor.
C. Deep-sea vent ecosystems thrive without sunlight by relying on chemical-based energy production.
D. Hydrogen sulfide is a chemical compound that is highly toxic to all living organisms.

questions.passage: The concept of sustainable architecture focuses on minimizing the negative environmental impact of buildings through efficiency and moderation. Architects achieve this by utilizing eco-friendly materials, optimizing energy and water consumption, and integrating renewable energy sources like solar panels. Beyond environmental benefits, sustainable buildings often improve indoor air quality and reduce long-term operational costs for owners. As urbanization accelerates globally, adopting these green building practices has transitioned from an ethical choice to an absolute necessity for future urban planning.
questions.question: What is the primary topic of this passage?
options: A. The financial breakdown of installing solar panels on corporate buildings.
B. An introduction to sustainable architecture, its methods, and its growing importance.
C. A historical review of how ancient cities managed their water systems.
D. The negative impacts of rapid global urbanization on natural habitats.

questions.passage: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), launched in December 2021, is the most powerful space observatory ever built. Operating primarily in the infrared spectrum, JWST allows astronomers to peer through cosmic dust clouds and look back in time to observe the very first galaxies formed after the Big Bang. The telescope features a massive gold-coated primary mirror measuring 6.5 meters in diameter, which collects significantly more light than its predecessor, the Hubble Space Telescope. Located about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth at a stable gravitational point known as L2, JWST continues to provide unprecedented images of deep space.

options: A. In December 2019
B. In December 2021
C. Exactly ten years after Hubble
D. It has not been launched yet

questions.passage: The Olympic Games originated in ancient Greece nearly 3,000 years ago as a religious festival honoring Zeus. The first recorded games took place in 776 BC in Olympia, featuring a single footrace won by a cook named Coroebus. The ancient games were held every four years until they were banned by Emperor Theodosius I in 393 AD due to their pagan associations. The tradition was revived centuries later in 1896, when the first modern Olympic Games were hosted in Athens, Greece, featuring 241 athletes from 14 nations competing in 43 events.

options: A. Emperor Theodosius I
B. A Greek priest from Olympia
C. A cook named Coroebus
D. One of the 241 modern athletes
